title: A La Carte (November 12)
summary: On spouses sitting together in church / Can’t you just be like me? / Husbands, pray for your wives / Six comforts for pastors / The most fun I ever had / Will we really be perfect in heaven? / The most offensive doctrine / Kindle deals and more See Also A La Carte (October 7) A La Carte (September 3) A La Carte (August 1)
content: I hope you don’t mind that this is a bit of a book-heavy week, but I’ve had a lot of book content I have wanted to share. Hence, we’ve had This Week in Christian Books , The First 100 Books for the Children’s Section of Your Church Library , and Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress . A book review will follow tomorrow, then we’ll be mostly caught up for now. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include P rioritizing the Church in Missions , Growing Up , and several good books for children. Recommended Reading On Spouses Sitting Together in Church. I happened to spot some of the kerfuffle that erupted after TGC Australia shared an article about why spouses should consider not sitting together in church. As happens on social media, the response seemed far out of proportion to the article. I found Murray Campbell’s response a good and reasonable one, even if I intend to keep sitting with Aileen most Sundays. Can’t You Just Be Like Me? I suppose in some ways, Bobby Scott’s piece on tribalism and disunity could nicely follow the previous article. “Tribalistic churches and Christians demand conformity to their broad range of preferences, believing they are inviolable God-ordained principles. So they strive to silence or coerce other Christians to assimilate, or they quietly despise these brothers and sisters. This inevitably leads to dark consequences. Instead of loving other Christians who have the same primary biblical convictions but differ over tertiary issues, tribalistic Christians feel justified in waging war against them.” Nelson’s Complete Book of Bible Maps and Charts is out in a fourth edition, updated with new high-resolution photography to go with its full-color maps, timelines, and charts for every book of the Bible. (Sponsored) Husbands, Pray for Your Wives. Costi Hinn: “I’ll never forget the first time I sat in a men’s Bible study on a Saturday morning listening to a man unpack the importance of praying for your wife. I was honestly blown away by the simplicity of it all and how I had never thought to pray for her — and I mean, like really pray for her.” He outlines eight ways men can do so. Six Comforts for Pastors. This article from Darryl Dash delivers what it promises. “If we base our identity on how well our ministries are going from an earthly perspective, we will be in trouble. Every pastor’s ministry will have good times and bad times. Basing our identity on how well things seem to be going is like putting our hope in a volatile stock. We will end up elated some of the time and despondent the rest. As pastors, we need to put our confidence in something more secure than how well things seem to be going. Here are six comforts for pastors that will last and sustain us, no matter how well or poorly our ministry seems to be going.” The Most Fun I Ever Had. Concerned about all those who are disparaging motherhood today, Brittany Allen chooses to celebrate it. “I still find it hard to write articles about the joys of motherhood because I never want to isolate sisters who are longing for a family. Yet, at the same time, I want to talk back to our culture that treats motherhood as a curse rather than a gift.” Will We Really Be Perfect in Heaven? Randy Alcorn: “Someone e-mailed me this question: ‘In Heaven, will some people still be annoying? After all, eternity’s a long time!’ Annoyance is sometimes caused by others’ sin, our own, or both. Since sin will be eliminated, so will annoyance. That doesn’t mean people won’t have idiosyncrasies, only that they won’t be rooted in sin, and none of us will degrade or dismiss others.” He explains what it means that we will be perfect in heaven. The Most Offensive Doctrine Every now and again, I like to share a quote that I have encountered through my reading. This is drawn from J.C. Ryle’s Expository Thoughts on Luke , which I’m enjoying a lot. Of all the doctrines of the Bible, none is so offensive to human nature as the doctrine of God’s sovereignty.

summary: A new serpent in the garden of Africa / On naming the dead / Why your favorite worship song’s grammar matters / 3 Reasons you should not date while watching porn / Would you forgive me of my narcissism? / Christianity Today and the sin of centrism / Kindle deals, videos, and more See Also A La Carte (June 27) Weekend A La Carte (October 25) Kindle Deals for Christian Readers
content: Good morning, my friends. The God of love and peace be with you today. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include Paul Tripp & Timothy Lane’s excellent Relationships: A Mess Worth Making , R.C. Sproul’s Growing in Holiness (which I don’t think I’ve seen on sale before), and Jonathan Landry Cruse’s What Happens When We Worship , among others. If you’d like to celebrate Advent with Spurgeon, Westminster Books has a deal on a new devotional book that may be of interest to you. If that’s not quite right for you, there’s lots of other resources in the Advent Sale . Recommended Reading A New Serpent in the Garden of Africa. “Just as the serpent led Adam and Eve into idolatry by reinterpreting God’s good word, so prosperity and word-of-faith preachers are today proclaiming a false and idolatrous gospel. But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology.” Dieudonné Tamfu writes from an African perspective and describes the importance of the recent Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . On Naming the Dead. Andrew Roycroft explains why it’s important that we not merely remember the dead, but name them. “The park bench copperplate, the trinkets and human ephemera that we treasure more than diamonds, the ongoing dedication of certain pieces of music truly matter, and keep back the dimming power of death for a time. Recently, in the wake of my friend’s death, I have been seeking to honour him by reading his favourite authors, enjoying afresh what I know he enjoyed and feeling a continued sense of fraternity and fellowship through these authors who meant so much to him.” Why Your Favorite Worship Song’s Grammar Matters. Porter C. Taylor explains why grammar matters when it comes to worship songs, and why the Psalms model the kind of worship that serves us best. “What if the worship wars have been fighting the wrong battle? What if contemporary worship music supplies a necessary register too often missing from our musical praise before our Creator? The question we should ask of our worship songs is not simply whether they make accurate statements about God. We should also ask what they enable the gathered church to say and do before God.” Nelson’s Complete Book of Bible Maps and Charts is out in a fourth edition, updated with new high-resolution photography to go with its full-color maps, timelines, and charts for every book of the Bible.  (Sponsored) 3 Reasons You Should Not Date While Watching Porn. I don’t think I am the only one who has been asked this question many times over: Should I refrain from dating until I am free from porn? Jacob Valk answers in the affirmative and offers three good reasons. Would You Forgive Me of My Narcissism? John Beeson explains why narcissism may not just be a problem that others have. “The most discussed personality disorder of our day is narcissism. A brief foray into Google Trends (always a fun rabbit hole to go down) shows that through the early 2000s, narcissism was searched about as often as some of the more well-known personality disorders. In 2015, that number began to rise and by 2022, it rocketed way above any other psychiatric disorder search. That aligns with my own experience as it is now a regular occurrence for me to hear a counselee accuse someone else of narcissism.” Christianity Today and the Sin of Centrism. title: This Week in Christian Books (November 10, 2026)
summary: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books. Here is a look at the Christian books that came our way this week, including Biblical and Theological Studies, From Silence to Sinai. See Also New and Notable Christian Books for October 2026 (Plus a Preview of November) This Week in Christian Books (October 27, 2026) Best Commentaries on Leviticus
content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. summary: C.S. Lewis's vices / How to graciously say no / Can’t you let me just attend? / When morningness is confused with godliness / Everyone doesn’t react the same way / Evangelizing with a dog / Kindle deals / New books See Also A La Carte (1/12) A La Carte (11/10) A La Carte (12/2)
content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. So this has become my nod to the need for daily exercise. Being one of the few beings on the planet who still buys a hard copy of a daily newspaper, I take my hound – a cocker spaniel with unusually short legs – with me of a morning. On the way, on most days at least, we pass a stand where two, sometimes three, Jehovah’s Witness ladies seek to engage people in conversation.” New Book Releases New Christian books tend to release on Tuesdays. title: Why Many Profess Christ but Don’t Possess Christ—and What It Means for Discipleship
summary: The gospel still changes everything. But have we embraced something less? The reason many profess Christ but don't possess Christ, and how a reduced understanding of the gospel can leave people mistaking religious activity for saving faith. See Also The Hard Work Is Done—Family Bible Study Is Fun Free-stuff Fridays (Truth78) Evangelize 2024: Growing a Church That Proclaims The Gospel
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get

title: What If Your Church Sings Hillsong and You Wish It Wouldn’t?
summary: A few weeks ago, I explained why my church does not sing songs by Hillsong, and, by the same convictions, songs by Bethel and Elevation. Today, a related matter: what should you do if your church sings Hillsong, but you wish it wouldn’t? See Also Why My Church Does Not Sing Songs by Bethel, Elevation, and Hillsong A La Carte (May 15) Weekend A La Carte (July 15)
content: A few weeks ago, I explained why my church does not sing songs by Hillsong , and, by the same convictions, songs by Bethel and Elevation. I tried to be clear that I do not understand this to be a matter of clear right or wrong, but rather a matter of wisdom and conscience. While this is a decision we have made for our church, I would not look down on churches that choose differently. I wish I had addressed a related matter at that time: what should you do if you see this issue in the way I do, but the leaders of your church do not? In other words, what should you do if your church sings Hillsong, but you wish it wouldn’t? I want to offer just a few thoughts on that. In general, I would suggest you just sing the songs, provided they do not require you to sing anything that is unbiblical. And thankfully, the majority of the songs by Hillsong, Bethel, and Elevation will not force you to sing error. That said, there are a few songs that may come close, or whose lyrics are imprecise enough that they could be understood in different ways. For example, Hillsong’s “So Will I (100 Billion X)” has these words in its second verse and the chorus that follows it: All nature and science Follow the sound of Your voice And as you speak A hundred billion creatures catch your breath Evolving in pursuit of what you said If it all reveals your nature so will I The most natural reading of those words is an affirmation of some kind of theistic evolution. I could not sing that, and I understand that you may not be able to either. Bethel’s “Reckless Love” continually ascribes recklessness to God. Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God Oh, it chases me down, fights ’til I’m found, leaves the ninety-nine I couldn’t earn it, I don’t deserve it, still You give Yourself away Oh, the overwhelming, never-ending, reckless love of God It is difficult for me ( and for John Piper , as it happens) to find a sense in which the word “reckless” is a fitting word for God. I think I know what the songwriters were hoping to convey with the word, but “reckless” is not suitable when speaking of God’s love and purposes, and I understand why many Christians could simply not permit themselves to sing it. I couldn’t either. But apart from those songs and a few others, most do not contain lyrics that are false or wrong. If your elders have deemed these songs suitable for your church, then it’s probably best to sing them in submission to the people whose leadership you have decided to follow. There is no “followership” in this world, other than following Christ, that does not at times involve submitting our own preferences to the preferences of our leaders. It would probably be a good time for a reminder that you just can’t have it all on this side of glory. Every pastor, every eldership, and every church will have both strengths and weaknesses. Too many Christians (who are also a bewildering collection of both strengths and weaknesses, of course) spend their whole lives searching for a perfect church, never quite grasping that it’s a futile effort. They go to the church with great preaching, but find that its evangelism is disappointing; they head for the church with great evangelism, but find its polity is poor. They soon switch again, this time choosing the church with their preferred polity, only to discover that it’s lacking in fellowship. They never learn the joy of settling into an imperfect church, in which they can rejoice in the strengths while bearing with the weaknesses. Sometimes accepting those weaknesses means singing songs or tolerating musical styles that are not aligned with their preferences, even when that’s hard to do. But what if the church does sing those songs that have actual errors in them? In the moment, I’d suggest you simply stop singing and refrain from making a big deal of it. You don’t need to make a fuss or storm out. But afterward, it would be wise to speak with your pastors to address your concerns, humbly, of course, and w
author: Tim Challies

title: A La Carte (November 9)
summary: Christianity under the progressive gaze / Why Christians must reject the conspiratorial mind / Wise people strive to be wiser / The pro-life movement’s midterm reckoning / How evil works / Preaching in paragraphs / Kindle deals / and more. See Also A La Carte (September 10) A La Carte (February 10) A La Carte (January 15)
content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several excellent biographies from Crossway. Each of them is good, but I’m partial to the one on R.C. Sproul. Note that these biographies are typically priced between $22 and $40. In case you missed it on the weekend, Westminster Books is offering a deep discount on the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . Recommended Reading Christianity Under the Progressive Gaze. Kyle Borg: “What interests me more than politics is the apparent cultural strength and growing respectability of progressive Christianity. In fact, a headline in The Guardian boldly declared: ‘A progressive understanding of Christianity won in the US elections.’ In a society where historic Christian convictions — and I don’t just mean Reformed confessionalism but basic creedal Christianity — is often treated with suspicion, if not hostility, some expressions of ‘Christianity’ seem to be enjoying a rather warm reception.” Counterfeit Providence: Why Christians Must Reject the Conspiratorial Mind. Mitchell Bahnsen explores the conspiratorial mind and explains why it’s so important for Christians to reject it. “None of this requires Christians to become gullible or naive. Psalm 2 describes kings taking counsel together against the Lord, and the crucifixion itself was a conspiracy carried out jointly by religious and governmental authorities. True connivance does occur, and wisdom to discern the truth is necessary in a complex and fallen world. However, we must defend against a totalizing hermeneutic of suspicion, lest it become its own form of faith.” Wise People Strive To Be Wiser. Justin Huffman discusses a principle that may be obvious, but is also important. “The wise person is always seeking to become wiser still. The truly spiritual person recognizes his or her constant need for spiritual growth.” The Pro-Life Movement’s Midterm Reckoning. First Things allows everyone to access several free articles per month, and this one from Jonathon Van Maren is worth one of the quota. He considers how the battle against abortion is likely to look very different after the midterm elections. “‘It’s impossible to sugarcoat it,’ Marjorie Dannenfelser of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America wrote in a memo issued on November 3. The 2026 midterm election results ‘are a disaster for the unborn, for their mothers, and for the country as a whole. Democrats are on track to control two of the three pieces they need to legalize taxpayer-funded abortion on demand, up until birth, in all fifty states—something they promise to start pushing as soon as they take office in January.'” How Evil Works. John Piper helpfully explains how evil works. “At the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfully accuse you of unforgiven sin in heaven, you will perish. And Jesus calls him ‘a murderer from the beginning’ (John 8:44). So, the deception and the accusation and the eternal death that results from unforgiven sin is a way of destroying people and opposing God.” Preaching in Paragraphs. This may be helpful for preachers to read as they let last week’s sermon fade into the past and begin to think about the next one. “Every preacher knows the terror of a blank screen. It is Tuesday morning—or even worse, Saturday afternoon—and the preacher sits and stares at his laptop. He has opened a new document in his word processor, and now the cursor stands idling on the page, patiently blinking. And the words aren’t coming.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re reading this via email, you’ll need to visit my site to fill out the form. Go here to read last week’s recommendations.) Submit
author: Tim Challies

title: Works & Wonders (November 8)
summary: This week’s Works & Wonders: the power of God, Nikon’s microscope photos, three Come, Thou Founts, a brain-injured musical genius, and Prepare Him Room live. See Also Works & Wonders: October 25 Works & Wonders (July 19) Works & Wonders (May 10)
content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: His Will Will Be Done Photomicrography Come, Thou Fount (×3) The Brain-Injured Musical Genius Grain from an Attic Prepare Him Room (Live) 1. His Will Will Be Done To have power is to have ability and strength. This is true whether the power belongs to human beings or to God himself—to creatures or to the Creator. Of course, our power is derived from God’s, but his is inherent. We are accountable to God for the way we use our power, but God is accountable only to himself. Our power is always small and incomplete, but God’s is always unbounded and unlimited. To say we are powerful is to say we possess the ability to do some of the things we desire some of the time. But to say God is powerful is to say God always possesses within himself the means necessary to bring about whatsoever he wills—to execute all his plans, to execute them all the way to perfect completion, and to overcome any and all resistance. This guarantees that God’s will will be done, for as the psalmist says, “Our God is in the heavens; he does all that he pleases” (Psalm 115:3). The God we worship today is the God for whom this is true: Whatever his will resolves and however his wisdom directs, his power will accomplish. 2. Photomicrography Shall we look at the results of another photography competition? Why yes, we shall. This week it’s Nikon’s Photomicrography Competition . “What is photomicrography you ask” (other than a word that is almost impossible to type correctly the first time, or even the fourth, in my case)? It is taking photos of microscopic objects and, in that way, opening a view to a world that is otherwise far too small for us to see. I think you’ll enjoy browsing the winners, which include spiders, pens, neurons, and inkjet printers. 3. Come, Thou Fount (×3) I really enjoy The National Parks and their delightful, easy-to-listen-to folk-Americana music. It’s my understanding that they grew up Mormon but have spoken openly about leaving that faith, but I am not aware of them becoming Christian. I was surprised, then, to see they had released a version of “ Come, Thou Fount .” It’s quite a good one. I’m not sure what motivated them to record it, but perhaps it was the same thing that motivated Marcus Mumford of Mumford & Sons, who has also recorded and performed it several times—I assume it was just the sheer beauty of the song. Mumford was raised in a Christian home, though later left the faith. His version is also wonderful. Another favorite rendition, sung by Christians, is this one by Celtic Worship . 4. The Brain-Injured Musical Genius The New York Times had an amazing feature this week, and it was amazing in two ways. First, it was beautifully put together with animated graphics and other visual elements. Second, it told a remarkable story—the story of a man who suffered a terrible brain injury but, through it, became a musical genius. I think you’ll enjoy reading The Brain Injury That Made a Middle School Teacher a Musical Genius . 5. Grain from an Attic Here’s a fun story from Italy that pastors may want to hang on to for future sermon illustrations. In the early 1990s, a farmer in Parma found some old seeds in his attic. He assumed they were useless, so he tossed them on the manure pile. Much to his surprise, they sprouted into a form of grain he had never seen before. I’ll leave you to read the story, look at the pictures, and consider the many possible illustrations and applications. Photo credit: Clara Vannucci 6. Prepare Him Room (Live) A couple of days ago, a friend told me that his children had begun listening to Christmas music, and we discussed whether it’s still too early in the year for that. We agreed that you don’t want to begin listening too early lest you grow tired of the relatively limited catalog of songs before Christma
author: Tim Challies

title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.

title: He found a Bible in a secondhand shop and thought he was the only Christian in Yemen
summary: 🇾🇪Yemen· 2000s
content: Mohammad grew up in Yemen, in a conservative Muslim home, in a country with almost no visible church at all. About seventeen years ago he found a Bible in a secondhand shop. He took it home and read it in hiding, because being caught with it could cost him everything. What he read pulled him in, and he gave his life to Jesus. Then came a strange loneliness. "When I came to faith, I thought I was the only believer in Yemen," he said. "For a long time, I didn't know any other Yemeni Christians." He was never actually alone He was wrong about being alone, and God kept proving it. Mohammad and his wife Alima, who came to Jesus after reading the Gospels herself, had been unable to have children for seven years. They prayed, and the infertility ended. Once, in a car accident, Mohammad says he saw a white light in the shape of a cross. Slowly he found other Yemeni believers, received discipleship, and today helps lead a house church in one of the hardest places on earth to follow Jesus. The man who thought he was the only one is now helping build a family of them. If you feel like the only believer in your world, take heart. Jesus is already gathering people you have not met yet, and He has not left you on your own.

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.

title: You can kill me, but you cannot take my faith in Jesus
summary: 🇧🇩Bangladesh· 2021-2022
content: Nur Alam and Afzal Hosen left Islam to follow Jesus in 2021, and they were baptised soon after. They did not keep it quiet. They wanted the Muslim community they came from to know the Jesus they had found, so they handed out Bibles and booklets around their part of Bangladesh. That is when the trouble started. A group seized Nur and locked him in a room for thirty hours, no food, no water, no sleep, demanding he return to Islam and threatening to kill him and his family. He would not bend. "At some point during the interrogation," Nur said, "they became hopeless, seeing my strong faith in Jesus." A faith they could not confiscate Days after Nur was freed, they came for Afzal. They beat him and accused him of being paid to convert. His answer has the ring of the early church about it. "You can kill me," he told them, "but you cannot take my faith in the Lord Jesus away from me." Both men were released, bruised and exhausted and still standing. They had discovered the thing every threat runs into eventually. You can take a man's freedom, his comfort, even his life, but the faith Jesus plants in a heart is not yours to seize. If Jesus is worth that to two young men in Bangladesh, He is worth your whole life too.

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.

title: He carried a bomb into a church. The sermon was about loving your enemies
summary: 🇮🇩Jakarta· 2000s
content: Ahmad Quraisy was a commanding officer in a militant Islamist group in Indonesia. The economic collapse of the late 1990s had radicalised him, and he blamed Christians for what had gone wrong. So he built a plan. He carried a time bomb into a Protestant church in Jakarta, intending to kill everyone inside. Then he heard the pastor preach. The man was telling his congregation to love their enemies and to pray for the people who persecuted them. Quraisy froze. "I never saw that Christian love before in my life," he said. He could not do it. He carried the bomb back out. His own leaders locked him up for a month for failing. The love he could not detonate That was only the beginning. In the year that followed, Quraisy began having visions he was sure came from Jesus. He was healed of typhus. His wife, unknown to him, had been quietly praying. By 2001 he gave his life to Christ. The man who wanted to blow up a church now builds them. Quraisy leads an underground network of around seven thousand former Muslims meeting in house churches across Indonesia, most of them still keeping a low profile to stay safe. The love that stopped his hand in that church is the same love reaching for you. It is stronger than the worst thing you ever planned to do.

title: He survived the killing fields. Then he baptised the man who ran a death camp
summary: 🇰🇭Cambodia· 1980s-1990s

title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s

title: His tough older brother went soft overnight. He had to know why
summary: 🇪🇹Ethiopia· 2010s

title: Boko Haram gave him a camera to break the church. He preached instead
summary: 🇳🇬Michika· 2020

title: He fled the ruins of Homs. In a dream, Someone came to save him
Locked in a cell a meter wide, he prayed one desperate sentence
summary: 🇮🇶Kurdistan· 2010s

title: He trained to be a Wahhabi sheikh and hated Christians. Then Jesus forgave him
summary: 🇪🇬Egypt· 2000s

title: He was ordered to execute a rival. Something he could not explain stopped his hand
summary: 🇬🇹Guatemala City· 2010s

title: Police shot him mid-escape. In that second he remembered what his mother said
summary: 🇧🇷Rio de Janeiro· 2010s

title: Kehilangan yang Membawa Berkah
title_zh: 带来祝福的失去
content: Oleh: Gevonny Dinda Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Gevonny Dinda, biasa dipanggil Dinda. Sebagai orang Kristen, saya merasa bersyukur dilahirkan di dunia ini dan berkesempatan untuk mengenal Tuhan Yesus. Saya sungguh bahagia dapat merasakan berkat-Nya setiap hari dan sangat bersyukur akan apa yang Tuhan Yesus berikan kepada saya selama ini. Kabar baik, kabar buruk, cobaan, dan berkat, saya terima dengan penuh rasa ucapan syukur. Di sini, saya akan menceritakan salah satu berkat Tuhan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada 19 Februari 2015, saya menerima kabar buruk bahwa kakek saya telah berpulang ke rumah Tuhan. Kepergian kakek saya sangat membekas di hati banyak orang, terutama nenek saya. Nenek saya sangat merasa kehilangan karena memang nenek belum siap menghadapi hal ini sehingga membuat kondisi badannya melemah. Sejak ditinggal kakek, kondisi mental dan fisik nenek saya semakin memburuk. Awalnya, ia merasa sangat kesepian dan merasa takut jika ditinggal sendirian di rumah. Bahkan, nenek saya sering menangis jika merasa kesepian. Ibu saya dan ketujuh saudara kandungnya akhirnya sepakat untuk bergantian menjaga nenek saya di rumahnya supaya tidak merasa kesepian lagi. Setelah itu, hari-hari nenek saya berjalan normal seperti biasa. Namun, karena umurnya yang bertambah tua, kondisi fisiknya semakin melemah. Sejak 2017, nenek saya sudah tidak kuat lagi berjalan dan harus memakai kursi roda. Di situlah, ketabahan dan kesabaran anak-anaknya, termasuk ibu saya, diuji dalam mengurus nenek saya. Pakde, budhe, tante, dan om saya yang hidup di luar kota, seperti: Jakarta, Yogyakarta, dan Kudus, semakin sering menyempatkan diri pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bergiliran mengurus nenek saya. Sampai pada April 2018 lalu, kondisi nenek saya berada di titik terburuknya. Karena anak-anaknya sudah memiliki firasat yang tidak baik, mereka memutuskan untuk berkunjung bersama-sama ke rumah nenek saya. Mereka hanya bisa berdoa bersama untuk kondisi ibu mereka. Sampai pada akhirnya, Tuhan Yesus memanggil nenek saya untuk ikut bersama-Nya. Karena sudah siap dengan kepergian nenek saya, kami semua menerima kepergian nenek dengan sukacita dan penuh ucapan syukur karena nenek saya sudah sembuh dan pergi ke tempat yang lebih indah, menyusul kakek saya. Tidak disangka, kepergian kakek dan nenek saya membawa berkah bagi keluarga besar kami. Tuhan Yesus memiliki kuasa untuk membuat keluarga kami menjadi lebih dekat satu sama lain. Hubungan anak-anak beserta cucu-cucu mereka menjadi lebih dekat. Kakak-kakak Ibu saya yang dahulu sering pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bertemu dan menjenguk orang tua mereka, sekarang lebih menghargai waktu kebersamaan dengan keluarga yang diberikan oleh Tuhan. Sejak saat itu, kami semua memiliki satu grup chat dan sering menanyakan kabar satu sama lain. Bahkan, kami semua memiliki keinginan untuk lebih sering bertemu pada masa depan, dan melakukan kegiatan bersama-sama seperti berlibur dan arisan keluarga. Semua itu tidak pernah terjadi sebelum kepergian kakek dan nenek saya, dan saya sungguh percaya Tuhan Yesus turut campur tangan dalam semua kejadian yang menimpa keluarga saya. Ia tidak pernah berhenti untuk menunjukkan betapa sayangnya Ia terhadap anak-anak-Nya, bahkan ketika anak-anak-Nya sedang berada dalam keterpurukan. Tuhan Yesus selalu memiliki rencana yang indah untuk setiap anak-anak-Nya, dan saya sangat percaya Ia telah memberikan sesuatu yang besar untuk membalas rasa kehilangan keluarga saya selama ini. Tuhan Yesus memang sungguh baik! Semoga Tuhan selalu memberkati keluarga Anda!

title: Berbagi dengan Mengajar dan Melayani
title_zh: 通过教学和侍奉来分享
content: Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Zefanya. Saya bersyukur karena pada kesempatan ini, saya dapat menyaksikan cinta kasih Tuhan yang Ia nyatakan melalui kegiatan mengajar bahasa Inggris yang saya lakukan secara volunter untuk anak-anak di beberapa desa di sekitar kota Salatiga. Kegiatan yang diselenggarakan oleh salah satu yayasan Kristen yang bergerak di bidang pelayanan dan pendidikan ini dilakukan setiap hari minggu. Pada kesempatan itu, saya beserta teman kuliah dan satu staf dari yayasan mendapat tugas untuk mengajar anak-anak di sebuah desa yang letaknya cukup jauh dari kota Salatiga, tempat kami tinggal. Butuh waktu sekitar dua jam lebih untuk sampai ke sana. Selama perjalanan, medan yang dilalui cukup sulit karena kami harus melewati jalanan aspal yang telah rusak parah dan jalanan tanah yang cukup sempit. Kami juga harus bersahabat dengan hawa panas yang sangat menyengat akibat dari teriknya sinar matahari ditambah dengan banyaknya tanah tandus dan pohon kering di sepanjang perjalanan. Namun, hal tersebut tidak mengurangi semangat kami untuk bertemu dengan anak-anak yang akan kami ajar. Setelah melalui perjalanan yang cukup melelahkan, akhirnya kami tiba di salah satu rumah warga yang akan kami gunakan untuk kegiatan belajar mengajar. Beberapa anak telah berkumpul di dalam rumah itu dan ketika mereka melihat kedatangan kami, mereka langsung membentuk barisan memanjang dan satu per satu mulai memberikan salam kepada kami. Alangkah manisnya! Saya sangat kagum dengan sikap mereka yang sangat ramah yang dapat membuat siapa saja ingin tersenyum ketika melihat mereka. Saya mulai mengajak mereka bercerita tentang pelajaran mereka di sekolah. Ada sekitar dua puluh anak yang datang untuk belajar. Usia mereka bervariasi, dari usia TK hingga SMP. Melalui percakapan mereka, saya mengetahui bahwa sebagian besar dari mereka belum pernah diajarkan bahasa Inggris di sekolah. Anak-anak SMP pun belum mengetahui pelajaran bahasa Inggris tingkat dasar seperti berhitung dari satu hingga sepuluh, atau menulis kosakata sederhana lainnya. Mereka juga bercerita tentang harapan mereka ke depan untuk memiliki fasilitas belajar yang memadai dan memperoleh lebih banyak kesempatan lagi untuk belajar bahasa Inggris. Hal itulah yang membuat kami sadar betapa mereka sangat ingin belajar hal-hal baru, tetapi fasilitas yang ada masih jauh dari kata memadai. Saya pun bersyukur karena dari kegiatan ini, mereka mendapat kesempatan untuk mempelajari hal-hal baru tersebut. Waktu belajar dimulai. Kami mengawalinya dengan berdoa, dan sebagian besar dari mereka, yang berbeda keyakinan, ikut melipat tangan dan menutup mata mereka. Selesai berdoa, kami membagi mereka dalam kelompok kelas kecil dan kelas besar. Kelas kecil terdiri dari anak usia TK hingga kelas tiga SD, sedangkan kelas besar terdiri dari anak-anak kelas empat SD ke atas. Saya mendapat kesempatan untuk mengajar anak-anak kelas besar. Banyak hal yang saya coba ajarkan kepada mereka, mulai dari kosakata sederhana tentang binatang, mengerjakan soal, hingga bermain gim sederhana untuk mengasah kemampuan bahasa Inggris mereka. Rasa lelah dan capai tentu kami rasakan karena mengajar anak-anak seusia mereka bukanlah perkara yang mudah. Namun, pada saat seperti itulah, kami menyadari bahwa kegiatan tersebut kami lakukan untuk memuliakan nama Tuhan. Kami yakin dan percaya bahwa Tuhanlah yang akan memberi kekuatan yang membuat kami mampu untuk melakukannya dengan baik. Kegiatan hari itupun selesai. Kami bersyukur bahwa kegiatan mengajar itu dapat kami lakukan dengan cukup baik terlepas dari kekurangan dan kendala yang kami rasakan sewaktu mengajar. Semangat belajar dari anak-anak juga membuat kami terdorong untuk memberikan pengajaran yang lebih baik lagi pada masa yang akan datang. Kami sangat bersyukur karena Tuhan memberikan perlindungan dan kasih-Nya kepada anak-anak yang kami ajar sehingga mereka masih dapat bertumbuh dengan baik dan memperoleh kesempatan-kesempatan untuk mengembangkan pengetahuan mereka. title: Tuhan Menuntunku Mengenal Pribadi-Nya
title_zh: 神引导我认识祂自己
content: Karena dilahirkan dan dibesarkan dalam keluarga Katolik Roma, saya dididik dengan segala tata cara mereka semenjak kecil. Sejak usia yang sangat muda, saya terbiasa mengakui dosa-dosa saya, dengan teguh percaya bahwa dosa-dosa saya diampuni pada waktu pengakuan dosa. Sering kali, beban dosa saya menjadi begitu besar sehingga setelah pengakuan dosa dan merasa bahwa dosa-dosa saya hilang, saya kemudian berharap untuk segera mati sebelum saya berbuat dosa lagi. Namun, pemikiran ini hanya sebentar karena hal itu hanya berlangsung beberapa menit sebelum saya kemudian berbuat dosa lagi, baik dalam pemikiran maupun tindakan. Pada waktu Paskah, selama pembacaan kisah penderitaan Kristus, semua penderitaan-Nya, dan akhirnya kematian-Nya, terkadang saya berpikir, "Mengapa Dia membiarkan mereka membunuh-Nya? Mengapa Dia tidak menghindar dari situasi itu?" Karena Dia adalah Allah, Dia dapat melakukannya. Namun, saya tidak mendapat jawaban. Sering kali, saya akan berpikir, "Apa yang akan saya katakan kepada Allah ketika saya bertemu Dia dengan semua dosa saya?" Sebagai seorang remaja, beban dosa saya sangat besar dan sangat berat bagi saya. Saya tidak tahu di mana saya akan berada dalam keabadian, dan orang-orang yang saya tanyakan memiliki kebingungan yang sama dengan saya. "Di mana jawabannya? Siapa yang memiliki jawabannya? Agama apa yang benar?" Saya bertanya. Namun, saya tidak pernah meragukan bahwa Gereja Katolik Roma adalah jalan yang benar. Hanya, saya tidak dapat menemukan kedamaian. Setelah saya menikah, keadaannya sama. Kemudian, saya memikirkan Alkitab. Meskipun saya belum pernah melihat ke dalamnya, saya tahu isinya akan benar. Firman Allah akan memiliki jawaban untuk saya, jawaban atas pertanyaan saya. Ke mana saya pergi: ke surga? Ke neraka? Bagaimana saya dapat mengetahuinya? Jika saya menuju surga, baiklah. Akan tetapi, jika saya menuju neraka, apakah ada yang bisa saya lakukan? Dan, selama masa-masa ini, saya menjadi semakin religius. Akhirnya, pada November 1975, saya menyuarakan keinginan saya untuk memiliki Alkitab, untuk membaca sendiri firman Tuhan. Suami saya berjanji untuk membelikan saya Alkitab sebagai hadiah Natal. Pada 8 Desember, dua pria yang dikenal oleh suami saya datang ke rumah kami, berbicara kepada kami tentang Tuhan Yesus Kristus, dan mengatakan bahwa mereka mengetahui dengan pasti bahwa mereka akan pergi ke surga, dan itu adalah menurut Alkitab. Mereka meninggalkan kami dengan sebuah buku Injil Yohanes, menunjukkan kepada kami satu atau dua ayat dari Alkitab, dan kemudian pergi. Salah satu dari ayat-ayat itu adalah "Sesungguhnya Aku mengatakan kepadamu, orang yang mendengar perkataan-Ku dan percaya kepada Dia yang mengutus Aku memiliki hidup kekal, dan tidak masuk ke dalam penghakiman karena ia sudah pindah dari kematian ke kehidupan" (Yohanes 5:24, AYT). Saya memikirkan betapa bahagianya orang-orang itu, yang secara pasti mengetahui tempat mereka akan menghabiskan kekekalan. Tepat seminggu kemudian, pada 15 Desember, pada larut malam, saya duduk dan membaca buku kecil lain yang saya dapatkan, God's Way of Salvation (Jalan Keselamatan Allah - Red.). Saya memahami dari buku tersebut bahwa meskipun keselamatan itu gratis bagi saya dan tidak dapat diperoleh dengan cara apa pun, itu tentu membuat Allah membayar dengan mahal. Dia telah memberikan Anak-Nya yang terkasih untuk mati bagi dosa di salib Kalvari. Namun, saya masih bingung bagaimana cara mendapatkan keselamatan ini. Kemudian, saya memikirkan hal-hal yang saya percayai untuk membawa saya ke surga: Agama saya, saya dorong keluar. Agama tidak dapat membantu saya. Baptisan saya, saya membuangnya. Baptisan tidak dapat memberi kedamaian kepada saya. Hidup saya yang baik, melakukan yang terbaik yang saya bisa, saya buang. Bahkan, kebaikan saya tidak dapat mengambil beban dosa saya. Doa saya, saya menyingkirkannya. Doa adalah perbuatan "saya" juga, dan itu bukanlah jawaban. Gereja saya. Bahkan, gereja saya yang sangat saya andalkan tidak dapat membuat sa

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Sebab itu, aku bagaikan tidak sadar ketika seorang serdadu tiba-tiba menarik aku. Dan meletakkan salib itu ke a

title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

title: Kembali Kepada Jalan Tuhan
title_zh: 回归主的道路
content: Nama saya Yoel, saya adalah seorang mahasiswa semester terakhir dari salah satu universitas swasta di Jawa Tengah. Saya dilahirkan dalam keluarga Kristen. Ibu dan Bapak saya cukup baik dalam membimbing saya untuk tetap dalam jalan Tuhan. Penyertaan Tuhan itu baik dalam kehidupan saya. Baiklah, saya akan ceritakan apa dosa yang sudah pernah saya lakukan. Rokok, pornografi, dan buang-buang waktu adalah keseharian saya pada waktu saya duduk di bangku SMU. Pada waktu itu, saya merasa ada yang kosong dalam hidup saya, tepatnya tidak ada gairah untuk mencapai suatu tujuan. Saya tidak merencanakan masa depan, pokoknya hidup terus mengalir. Sebenarnya, saya tertarik dengan dunia perfilman, saya ingin menjadi sutradara, tetapi ayah saya tidak mengizinkannya karena dia tidak melihat ada bakat seni dalam diri saya. Menurutnya, orang seni hanya akan mendapat uang atau pengakuan jika karyanya diterima. Kalau tidak mendapat pengakuan, ya "habis". Itulah perkataan ayah saya, saya masih ingat jelas. Menurut saya, dosa itu nikmat. Namun, saya juga sadar bahwa itu hanya kenikmatan sesaat.
